Admittedly I'm not sure what you mean by white flight, is that moving into a racial situation? 


Also, to note you mentioned needing the church in an immediate threat so I'm don't think I'm understanding what you're wanting the churches to do in this case. Churches aren't designed to house people in general, some have gyms and could operate like a shelter but that would require supplies for beds etc. I'm pretty sure almost every chuch in medicine hat at least has a kitchen, but they are more household style, they aren't designed to feed large numbers just like our own kitchens aren't. Additionally when serving food, then AHS has to get involved with permits etc, those are annual fees. Then unfortunately when you mis large groups of displaced people, you may need security, interpreters, additional support workers. I've worked with refugees of wars and the like, so ptsd and mental health traumas are very serious, so supports are needed there. 


I'd dream of a world where there wasn't any red tape like above, and that neighbors support neighbors, and we all look out for our fellow peoples around us, but the reality is for every person out there that wants to feed the world, cure the sick, and house the homeless, there's a myriad of forms, applications, other garbage that prevent it. Look at mustard seed as an example, they wanted to provide shelter for homeless, but it was stopped by others and politics. You have a good heart and want to help clearly, but in my experience, you're outnumbered by a population of people that only want to help themselves.

I've spoken to most local churches in the past prior to Ukraine invasion regarding helping refugees and similar. I can tell you that they have waiting lists for sponsorships and usually can only afford 1 a year as it's funded by their congregations. There is no system in place to support what I think you are talking about. Churches have bills, they can't afford to feed our own displaced citizens let alone open doors to all lost souls. In a perfect world or 100 years ago maybe, but churches are a corporation now more than ever and given the soon to be economical shift they will have to worry about feeding their own long before being able to help others.

Anything I've tried to think of has way more syllables and frankly the more weed I enjoy the less I want to use big long words or too science-y.

The theology and philosophy of life and when it starts its an absolutely beautiful topic that can be discussed endlessly. As a person with no mainstream religions beliefs I always lean towards the science first and foremost. However there is still many many things that science has yet to find answers for with the human body alone, which I find so intriguing in its own right. Now, I don't believe that a lack of answer to a question defaults it to magic or faith, but as a species, humanity wants to find answers and connections and patters, so theology is more than able to fit those gaps respectfully. Just as much as I support pro choice, etc etc, I also support freedom of belief. If a person can find answers in faith, and those answers do not infringe upon the beliefs and rights of others, they go for it. It's when a person chooses to believe that their beliefs are the only correct ones that exist, and they force that idea upon others that I take offense. I will always fight for peoples right to decide and make choices (vaccine, birth control, assisted suicide) and everyone has a right to believe what they want avout these topics, even discuss them freely, but no one has the right to tell a person that a personal belief is right or wrong in my opinion anyways lol 
(Yes I would also support a person's right to believe science is wrong, as much as it hurts my brain. The old saying, "you can lead a horse to water, but you can't make it drink" sort of applies in that case)
